note: Torah LM2 #121 (reference 1121) has zero bechina edges in the dataset. No edges of any type are recorded for reference 1121 in torahData.js. The source text is a short practical oral teaching (5 lines) about how to pray when prayer feels impossible. Its structure is entirely eitza-based advice: the Rebbe counsels breaking prayer into small sections, focusing on one segment at a time with kavana, so as not to be overwhelmed. The teaching does not develop any explicit 'X הוא בחינת Y' equations that would generate bechina edges. The single use of bechina language in the text — 'כָּל אֶחָד מִתְפַּלֵּל אֵיזֶה חֵלֶק מֵהַתְּפִלָּה לְפִי בְּחִינָתוֹ' — is grammatical ('according to their level'), not a structural equation identifying two concepts as parallel expressions of the same nature. No bechina-based packages can be constructed from the dataset for this Torah.
